## Installing models

A model is a directory in the models directory, named for the model's id.
There are three ways to get one: fetch a build sidekick publishes, download
one by hand, or convert the model yourself. Whichever you choose, restart
the daemon afterwards.

### Which models are published

`sidekickd fetch` installs only builds that sidekick has published on
Hugging Face and recorded in its checksum ledger. Not every model is: a
model's licence tier decides whether it may be published
([PUBLISHING.md](PUBLISHING.md#what-is-published-licence-tiers)), and
builds are published one release at a time. Each backend's build of a
model is published on its own, in its own repository
(`sidekickd/<model>-coreml`, `sidekickd/<model>-onnx`), so a model can
have a Core ML build to fetch, an ONNX build, or both; `--backend` picks
one (the default is Core ML on macOS and ONNX on Linux). The list of
published builds, each with its backend, is generated from the ledger in
[MODELS.md](MODELS.md#published-builds). A model or backend not listed
there is installed by converting it ([CONVERTING.md](CONVERTING.md)).

### Fetching a published build

`sidekickd fetch` downloads a build
sidekick publishes on Hugging Face ([PUBLISHING.md](PUBLISHING.md)),
verifies every file, and installs it in the models directory ([D51](DECISIONS.md#d51--sidekickd-fetch-the-hugging-face-cache-verified-installed-as-hard-links)). It
fetches the builds in [the published list](MODELS.md#published-builds):

```sh
sidekickd fetch bge-small-en-v1.5                     # its Core ML build on macOS; its ONNX build on Linux
sidekickd fetch bge-small-en-v1.5 --buckets 128,256   # only the buckets for inputs up to 256 tokens
sidekickd fetch bge-small-en-v1.5 --backend onnx      # its ONNX build, on any OS (an Intel Mac included)
sidekickd fetch <model> --accept-terms <model>        # a gated build (the Gemma models): accept its terms
```

The ledger records where and at which revision each build was published,
so the model id is enough; `--repo` and `--revision` name another
repository or revision (a build not published yet needs `--repo`).

- **Downloads go into the Hugging Face cache,** through the `hf` CLI when
  it's installed (its token, Xet transfers and settings, such as `HF_HOME`,
  `HF_HUB_CACHE` and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`), else by sidekickd itself, anonymously
  through `curl`, into the same cache in the same layout. Each sees the
  other's downloads as cached. A gated repository needs `hf`, signed in to
  an account that accepted its terms on the Hub.
- **Every file is verified** against the Hub's hash for it and against
  sidekick's checksum ledger, which is built into sidekickd. A file that
  matches neither is refused.
- **The model directory is hard links to the cached files,** so the model
  takes no more disk than the cache does, and deleting either one leaves
  the other whole. Not symlinks, as a Hugging Face snapshot's are: a
  program whose files link out of its directory can run off the ANE
  without an error
  ([design/coreml-cache.md](design/coreml-cache.md#symlinks-and-the-fallback-loader)).
  Where the cache is on another volume, the files are copied.
- **`--buckets` fetches part of a Cor

**The 0.985 gate.** It stays the converters' acceptance gate on their own
parity sets; the EmbeddingGemma, LFM2.5, F2LLM and gte-modernbert converters

A D on the adversarial corpus doesn't remove a model: the grade is

**Not done.**
- Per-token grading for models whose token vectors are the product (laya,
  ColBERT). Every registry model pools inside its graph, so the suite can't
  see per-token vectors.
- Parity through the HTTP layer.
- A corpus case built to maximize ModernBERT's massive activation, so the
  suite exercises the ANE linear's 2^15 limit (D25 amendment). Adding it
  means regenerating every reference.

**Amendment (October 2026): bucket invariance is sampled for buckets over
512 tokens.** Re-running every case in every larger bucket doesn't scale to
2,048-token buckets. For Lumma-fev (2,630 cases, ~1.24 s per ANE prediction
at 2,048) it alone took 2–3 hours, past the suite's time limit. With
`--bucket-invariance auto` (the default), a model whose largest bucket is
over 512 re-runs every case in its next larger bucket, and the adversarial
cases plus every 10th case in every larger bucket; `full` restores the old
behavior. That keeps the gate's two purposes:
- A bucket-specific defect shows on any input in that bucket, and every
  bucket still sees every case just below it plus the sample.
- A mask or position defect shows in any larger bucket, and every case is
  still checked one bucket up.
What it gives up is narrow: a defect that appears only two or more buckets
up, only for inputs outside the sample and the adversarial cases, and never
in the next bucket. Every model graded before this keeps full coverage and
an unchanged report, and the report prints the coverage it used.

**Amendment (October 2026, v0.8.0): ONNX is a graded path.** With D40's
backend, three points above no longer hold as written:
- `onnx-cpu` is graded, not report-only. It runs natively through
  `OnnxEmbedder`, the daemon's own code path, in a build with the `onnx`
  feature (on macOS or Linux), and has floors for the M1 Max (ONNX
  Runtime 1.28.3) and the Xeon W-3235 (1.23.2). `--external` grades
  vectors produced elsewhere as a cross-check. Published exports still
  run at reference time, as before.
- Not every path goes through `CoremlEmbedder`: an onnx model goes
  through `OnnxEmbedder`, with the same prefix, tokenizer, truncation,
  pooling and normalization, and no buckets or padding.
- Not every registry model pools inside its graph: an ONNX graph with
  token-level output is pooled in Rust. The suite still sees only the
  pooled vector.

The Core ML gates (compute plans, bucket invariance, ANE determinism)
don't apply to an onnx model, which has no plan and no buckets.

**Amendment (October 2026): one definition of the letters.** The grade
scales had been written out separately in the suite's code, in MODELS.md,
on the comparison page and in this log. The published letters were stored
by hand beside the numbers that should determine them, so they could drift
apart, and they had: the data and MODELS.md's Intel table graded one model
differently. Now:
- **The scales are `[grades]` in `fixtures/parity/expectations.toml`:** the
  embedders' cosine scale, the classifiers' |Δp| scale, and the ratio to
  the fp16 ceiling. The suite reads them, and so does
  `tools/models_table.py`, which generates MODELS.md's legends and puts the
  scales in `docs/data/models.json` for the comparison page's legend. The
  thresholds quoted elsewhere in this log are history, not the definition.
- **No published letter is stored by hand.** The generator computes each
  row's letter from its numbers: worst error, ratio, graded flips and

parity suite before relying on it. On macOS 27, a Core ML artifact whose
inputs accept several enumerated shapes can abort the process at its first
prediction, with an exception nothing can catch. With the dylib, that
process is your host app. So on macOS 27 sidekick refuses to load such a
model: `sk_embed` returns NULL with an error naming the input, and the
daemon answers with an error. Other flexible-shape artifacts load with a
warning and run on the CPU, off the ANE. `ane_check` rejects all of them
without running them (docs/MODELS.md, [D27](DECISIONS.md#d27--refuse-multi-shape-core-ml-models-at-load-on-macos-27)).

## Path 1: the daemon

**Authentication.** A daemon configured with an `api_key` requires
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` on every route except `/health` ([D13](DECISIONS.md#d13--default-bind-1270018790-health-unauthenticated)), so a
probe that reads `/v1/models` without the key gets a 401 with code
`invalid_api_key`. `/health` stays open: probe it first, and treat a 401
from the routes after it as "configured, but not for this client".

Every route, field and error is in [API.md](API.md): chat, embeddings
(`input_type`, `prompt_name`, `dimensions`, `encoding_format`,
`truncate`) and classification ([below](#classification)). What a host
needs beyond that:

**Prompts.** sidekick puts the model's own prompt before every input
([API.md](API.md#prompts)). A host that brings its own (an MTEB task
prompt, or a Qwen3-Embedding or F2LLM instruction for a symmetric task, in
the format [MODELS.md](MODELS.md#named-prompts-prompt_name) gives) sends
`input_type: "none"`, or a `prompt_name` the model lists in `/v1/models`
([API.md](API.md#named-prompts)). With `none`, truncate with `END` or keep
inputs within the limit: `START` can cut a prompt sidekick can't tell from
the text. Over the C ABI, `sk_embed`'s purpose 2 is `none`,
`sk_embed_named` takes a name where `sk_embed` takes a purpose, and
`sk_model_info` reports `prompts` and `named_prompts`.

**Over-length input.** `/v1/embeddings` refuses an input over the model's
limit with a 400, and refuses the whole request: split or shorten that
input and send the batch again
([API.md](API.md#input-length-and-truncation)). To know before
embedding, send `POST /tokenize` with the `input_type` you will embed
with: its `fits` is the route's own check ([API.md](API.md#tokenize)).
Use it rather than a tokenizer or a character estimate of your own, which
can disagree at the edge. A client that truncates some documents on
purpose can send `/tokenize` first, log the ones that don't fit, with
their counts, and send those with `truncate: "END"`.

**The two paths differ here.** The library's own default stays `END`:
`sk_embed` has no `truncate` parameter and always truncates, as does the
Rust `Embedder::embed`. `sk_model_info` reports each model's
`max_seq_len`. A host that follows the probe order above (daemon, else
dylib) should send `truncate: "END"` to the daemon to get the same vectors
on both paths, or handle both behaviours: a 400 from the daemon, and a
silently truncated vector from the dylib.

To make "installed but not running" disappear entirely, install the
LaunchAgent ([INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#running-as-a-service); `KeepAlive`
keeps it running); then path 2 only matters for machines where the user
skipped that step. On Linux, run sidekickd under your service manager; no
unit file ships.

## Path 2: `libsidekick.dylib`

[`crates/sidekick-embed-ffi/include/sidekick.h`](../crates/sidekick-embed-ffi/include/sidekick.h);

`target/release/libsidekick.dylib` (~5 MB, embeddings only, no
FoundationModels linkage — it runs Core ML and static models on any macOS
they run on). Releases ship it only in the Apple silicon archive.

**Compiled models are cached under your app's identity, not sidekickd's.**

## ONNX Runtime on the CPU (`onnx-cpu`)

sidekick's `onnx` backend (D40) serves the same embedders through ONNX
Runtime on the CPU of any supported platform: one fp32 `model.onnx` per
model, exported by the conversion library (`--format onnx`, see
docs/CONVERTING.md) from the same checkpoint and gated against the same
fp32 references, or fp16 weights computed in fp32 (`--onnx-weights fp16`).
It serves embedders only: classifiers and rerankers are Core ML only. At
scan time the daemon checks the graph's inputs and outputs against the
manifest's `[io]`, marks a quantized graph (run one input at a time), and
keeps external weight data inside the model's directory. The parity suite
grades it as the `onnx-cpu` path.

### Accuracy

Graded natively on the shipped runtimes, 51-case corpus: ONNX Runtime
1.28.3 on an Apple M1 Max and an Apple M4 Max (macOS, arm64), an AMD
Ryzen 7 5800X and an AMD Threadripper 3970X (Linux, x86-64), and 1.23.2
on an Intel Xeon W-3235 (macOS, x86-64), there with ONNX Runtime's AVX-512 kernels (D42).
onnx-cpu cells give 1 − the worst-case cosine; the
Threadripper's grades match the Ryzen's bit for bit, so they share a
column. The Core ML columns are the Apple paths from the table above.
